The NVIDIA SimReady post (history_match related to 09-18 'AI agents to prepare 3D scenes') is kept as distinct content: it covers converting CAD assets into SimReady OpenUSD assets with materials, collisions and joints set by frontier models, while the 09-18 post covered scene preparation by agents. It is the weakest pick. Dropped: Nikon Small World in Motion (owned by movies); Google Playground (owned by games); Fanta AI Halloween ad (advertising critique, fits marketing better, same call as 10-09); Creative Bloq indie game Limerence (avoids gen AI, so AI is not what makes the story); Matt Wolfe roundup (bundles Haiku 5.5 and ChatGPT Intelligent UI, which was already published 10-08); AI Advantage Claude for Workspace short (a short clip on the Claude Docs/Slides thread from 09-17, no new release identified); MindStudio Stitch 2.0, Stitch MCP and Seedance intro posts (SEO-style vendor walkthroughs, related to the Stitch 09-28 card); Figma Sightlines no.3, Eleken AI-native UX, and UX Collective essays on AI UI, synthetic users and Tesler's Law (generic opinion with no concrete release); Boston Dynamics hand (AI is not central); DEV Blender stack post (related to 09-28 'Claude helped me make this animated video in Blender', running theme). items.rationale: A new integration: animated explainers made in Claude Motion export straight into Runway for footage generation, voiceover, music, scene edits and channel reformatting. It turns a two-tool motion workflow into one pipeline.
items.excerpt: Runway now integrates with Claude Motion: export animated explainers from Claude into Runway to generate footage, add voiceover and music, edit scene by scene and reformat for every channel.

items.rationale: A new launch: AWS's open-source Physical AI toolchain gives product and robotics engineers reference architectures for simulation, training and deployment.
items.excerpt: AWS launched an open-source Physical AI toolchain with reference architectures for simulation, training and deployment, aimed at robotics and product engineering teams.

items.rationale: A hands-on test of the Instinct AI agent's interface against Muse and ChatGPT Dots. It is a concrete read on which agent UX patterns hold up as competition grows.
items.excerpt: A hands-on with Instinct, last season's buzziest AI agent, and whether its interface and experience can survive new competition from Muse and ChatGPT Dots.

items.rationale: A five-step NVIDIA method that uses frontier AI models to turn CAD assets into SimReady OpenUSD assets with materials, collisions and joints, so 3D designers can hand off simulation-ready assets.
items.excerpt: NVIDIA shows five steps for using frontier AI models to turn CAD assets into SimReady OpenUSD assets, configuring materials, collisions and joints for robotics simulation.

items.rationale: Explains why coding agents that screenshot-diff against a Figma frame keep thrashing, and shows that comparing layout geometry gives faithful AI-built UIs. Teams can apply the fix to design-to-code loops right away.
items.excerpt: Why pointing a coding agent at a Figma frame and screenshot-diffing until it 'matches' thrashes, and how comparing layout geometry instead produces faithful AI-built UIs.
